agentOverflow.title: Agent-overflowtoewijzing
agentOverflow.tooltip: Configureer hoe vrije agents worden verdeeld zodra elke taak op elke prioriteitsniveau zijn max_agents-limiet heeft bereikt.
agentOverflow.priorityFifoDescription: Wanneer meerdere taken met dezelfde prioriteit hun max_agents-limieten overschrijden, ontvangt de oudste taak (eerst aangemaakt) alle extra agents.

agentOverflow.enforceMaxAgentsDescription: Strictly cap each job at its max_agents limit — no overflow. Surplus agents stay idle. Most predictable; can waste capacity.
agentOverflow.maxAgentsFifoDescription: All jobs at all priorities fill to max_agents first (strict caps). Any remaining agents then pile on the OLDEST job overall — bypassing priority. Maximizes throughput while still giving every job its baseline.
agentOverflow.maxAgentsRoundRobinDescription: All jobs at all priorities fill to max_agents first (strict caps). Any remaining agents then rotate evenly across ALL jobs — bypassing priority. Maximizes throughput with fair distribution beyond the baseline.

intro.title: Cloud GPU provisioning
intro.body: Rent GPU instances on demand when the on-prem fleet cannot keep up. Instances join your existing VPN, receive only the files their job needs, and are torn down automatically. Spend is committed against a per-client budget before an instance boots, so a cap is a real limit rather than an after-the-fact measurement.

providers.title: Cloud providers
providers.description: Where rented instances come from, and how they reach this server.
providers.deleteBody: Delete "{{name}}"? This fails while any rented instance still references it.
providers.empty: No cloud providers configured. Nothing will be rented.
providers.preflightFailedBody: This provider cannot launch instances yet.

preflightSections.inconclusive: Could not be verified (treated as failure)

ackBody.vastai: Vast.ai verhuurt GPU’s op particuliere machines waarvan de beheerders root-toegang tot de container hebben. Hashes, woordenlijsten en gekraakte wachtwoorden die daar worden geplaatst zijn zichtbaar voor een derde partij. Dit verschilt fundamenteel van AWS of RunPod Secure Cloud, waar instances in uw eigen account of in SOC 2-datacenters draaien.
ackBody.runpod_community: RunPod Community Cloud verhuurt GPU’s op machines van derden waarvan de eigenaren root-toegang tot de container hebben. Hashes, woordenlijsten en gekraakte wachtwoorden die daar worden geplaatst zijn zichtbaar voor een derde partij. De verklaringen van RunPod gelden alleen voor Secure Cloud en strekken zich niet uit tot dit niveau.

providers.ackConfirm: Do you accept this exposure for workloads sent to this provider?
providers.ephemeralKeyBody: KH_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set, so a random key was generated at startup. Every stored credential becomes unreadable after the next restart. Set KH_ENCRYPTION_KEY before saving provider credentials.
providers.vpnSectionHelp: This server is never exposed to the internet, so rented instances join the VPN you already run. OpenVPN is not supported: it needs /dev/net/tun and CAP_NET_ADMIN, which Vast.ai's unprivileged containers do not provide.

reusableKeyWarning.tailscale: A reusable key is shared by every instance and expires — Tailscale caps auth keys at 90 days. Once it lapses, provisioning is refused rather than launching instances that cannot connect. An OAuth client lets KrakenHashes mint a single-use ephemeral tagged key per instance instead.
reusableKeyWarning.netbird: A reusable setup key is shared by every instance, so the same secret reaches every rented host. Set Credential expires at below if the key has an expiry — provisioning is then refused once it lapses instead of launching instances that cannot connect; leave it blank for a key that never expires. Tag or group is ignored for this credential type: the group and the ephemeral flag come from the key's own configuration in NetBird. An access token lets KrakenHashes mint a single-use ephemeral setup key per instance and set the group itself.

providers.staticConfigWarning: WireGuard uses a static peer config: there is no per-instance credential and no automatic deregistration when an instance dies. Tailscale or NetBird is safer.

credentialKinds.oauth: OAuth client — mint one ephemeral key per instance (recommended)
credentialKinds.pat: Access token — mint one ephemeral key per instance (recommended)
credentialKinds.reusable_key: Reusable key — shared by every instance

vpnCredentialHelp.oauth: Tailscale OAuth client as client_id:client_secret. Needs the auth_keys scope and the tag selected.
vpnCredentialHelp.pat: NetBird personal access token or service-user token.
vpnCredentialHelp.reusable_key: The pre-authorized key every instance will use.

fields.name: Name
fields.credentialsHelp: API credentials for {{provider}}. Stored encrypted and never returned.
fields.credentialsKeepHelp: Leave blank to keep the stored credential unchanged.
fields.maxHourlyHelp: Offers above this rate are never rented, whatever the budget allows.
fields.credentialExpiryHelp: Optional — leave blank for a key that never expires. Provisioning is refused after this time, and you will be warned as it approaches.
fields.vpnTagHelp: e.g. tag:kraken-worker. Required for Tailscale OAuth; scopes what these nodes may reach.
fields.backendVpnHost: This server's address on the VPN
fields.backendVpnHostHelp: The KH_HOST value cloud agents use. The server certificate must cover it — add it under the Server Certificate tab and click Apply & Reissue, or agents will fail TLS hostname verification.
fields.awsAccessKeyIdHelp: An IAM user or role key scoped to EC2 provisioning. Stored encrypted and never returned.
fields.awsRegionHelp: e.g. us-east-2. Every other AWS field below must live in this region.
fields.awsSubnetHelp: e.g. subnet-0abc123. Must auto-assign a public IP, or the instance cannot reach your VPN's control plane.
fields.awsSecurityGroupsHelp: Comma-separated, e.g. sg-0abc123. Needs outbound access only; no inbound rule is required.
fields.awsAmiSsmHelp: Resolved at launch, so the image never goes stale. e.g. /aws/service/deeplearning/ami/x86_64/base-oss-nvidia-driver-gpu-ubuntu-22.04/latest/ami-id
fields.awsAmiIdHelp: Pin a specific image instead. Leave blank to resolve through SSM. One of the two is required.
fields.awsInstanceProfileHelp: Optional. Only needed if the agent itself must call AWS APIs.
fields.awsRootVolumeHelp: A floor; a job's file set may need more. Must be at least the AMI's snapshot size or the launch fails.
fields.awsEbsRateHelp: gp3 storage price. Left at 0 the budget reserves nothing for disk.
fields.awsUseSpotHelp: Spot requests are one-time and terminate on interruption. Discounts on current-generation GPU are often modest, so this is not automatically cheaper. Spot and on-demand draw on separate vCPU quotas.
fields.mockAgentBinaryHelp: Path to an agent binary the server can execute with --test-mode.
fields.mockDropLaunchResponse: Fault: drop the launch response (instance runs but is reported failed)
fields.vpnTagIgnoredHelp: Ignored for a NetBird reusable key: group membership and the ephemeral flag come from the setup key's own configuration in NetBird. Used only on the access-token path, as auto_groups on each minted key.

vpnUrlHelp.netbird: Your self-hosted NetBird management server, e.g. https://netbird.example.com. Used both to mint setup keys and to start the client. Leave blank for NetBird's hosted service.
vpnUrlHelp.tailscale: Only for a self-hosted control server. Note that access-token minting always uses api.tailscale.com and does not support Headscale.

peerWarningBody.vastai: Vast.ai-instances draaien op particuliere machines die u niet beheert. Schakel dit alleen in voor klanten van wie de gegevens aan derden mogen worden blootgesteld, en bevestig dit ook per klant.
peerWarningBody.runpod_community: RunPod Community Cloud draait op machines van derden waarvan de eigenaren root-toegang tot de container hebben. De SOC 2-, ISO 27001- en PCI DSS-verklaringen van RunPod gelden alleen voor Secure Cloud, niet voor dit niveau. Schakel dit alleen in voor klanten van wie de gegevens aan derden mogen worden blootgesteld, en bevestig dit ook per klant.

providers.awsSectionHelp: Where instances launch and what they cost. EC2 exposes no machine-readable GPU model or hourly rate to this code, so both are declared here.
providers.awsInstanceTypesHelp: Only the types listed here can be rented. Declare the rate you are willing to be billed at — round up, since the budget reserves against this number and nothing cross-checks it against an invoice. Declaring the GPU model and count is what enables cost-per-work ranking; without it, ranking falls back to price per hour.
providers.mockSectionHelp: The mock provider spawns local agent --test-mode processes. The fault toggles exercise failure branches without recompiling.
providers.providerNotImplemented: This provider has no adapter yet: the backend rejects it with "unsupported cloud provider" at launch time. It can be saved, but nothing can be provisioned from it.

budgets.title: Client budgets
budgets.description: What each client may spend, and which providers their data may go to. Clients with blank fields follow the server defaults below.
budgets.empty: No clients exist yet. Create a client first, then fund it here.
budgets.saveFailed: Failed to save client cloud settings
budgets.ackTitle: Acknowledge third-party exposure for this client
budgets.ackWarningTitle: This client's data would leave your control
budgets.ackWarningBody: Allowing Vast.ai for {{name}} means this client's hashes, wordlists and cracked plaintexts may be placed on machines owned by third parties who have root access to the container.
budgets.ackConfirm: Do you accept this exposure for this client?

fields.budgetHelp: Spend ceiling for the current budget period. Leave blank to inherit the server default; a client only ends up unfunded if no default is set either.
fields.ttlHelp: An instance is destroyed at this age regardless of progress. Leave blank to use the system default.
fields.providersHelp: Empty means nothing may be rented for this client. Allowing AWS while forbidding Vast.ai is a normal configuration.
fields.periodHelp: Leave blank to inherit the server default.

errors.invalidBudget: Budget must be a number, e.g. 25.00
errors.invalidTtl: Maximum lifetime must be a positive number of minutes
errors.enabledWithoutBudget: Set a budget before enabling cloud burst — an unfunded client can never provision anything.
errors.enabledWithoutProvider: Allow at least one provider before enabling cloud burst.

budgets.peerTooltip: Hardware van derden: de eigenaar van de machine kan de gegevens van deze klant lezen.

defaults.title: Server defaults
defaults.description: Values a client uses when it has not set its own. Leaving a client's field blank means it follows the default here, so changing this changes every client still inheriting.
defaults.summaryUnset: No default budget set — clients that inherit stay unfunded
defaults.budgetHelp: Leave blank for no default: inheriting clients then stay unfunded and cannot burst.
defaults.enabled: Clients may burst to paid capacity by default
defaults.providersHelp: Applied to any client whose own provider list is empty.
defaults.peerAckNote: Peer-operated providers still require a per-client acknowledgement. Defaulting them in does not grant that consent — each client must still be acknowledged individually before its data can go there.
defaults.appliesNow: Cloud burst is enabled by default and a default budget is set, so every client still inheriting can now provision paid capacity.
defaults.fundedButDisabled: A default budget is set but cloud burst is off by default, so no inheriting client can provision anything. Tick the box above to make the budget usable.
defaults.enabledWithoutProviders: Cloud burst is on by default but no default providers are selected, so inheriting clients still cannot rent anything. Choose at least one provider above.
defaults.willEnableTitle: This will let {{count}} client(s) rent paid capacity
defaults.willEnableBody: These clients have no settings of their own, so they follow the defaults above. Saving lets each of them provision cloud instances and spend against this budget. To keep a client out, set its own Cloud burst to Disabled.
defaults.confirmBody: {{count}} client(s) currently cannot rent anything. Saving these defaults gives each of them a {{amount}} ceiling per {{period}} and permission to spend it. The budget is per client, not shared, so this is the total exposure multiplied by the number of clients listed.
defaults.confirmAlternative: Prefer to opt in one at a time? Cancel, leave cloud burst off by default, and set Cloud burst and a budget on each client individually instead.

policy.title: Spend threshold policy
policy.description: What happens as a client approaches its cap. These thresholds decide how gracefully the cap is reached; what actually prevents an overrun is that an instance's whole lifetime cost is committed before it boots.
policy.loadFailed: Failed to load the threshold policy
policy.saveFailed: Failed to save the threshold policy
policy.overageWarning: Overage is allowed: reservations may exceed the remaining budget. The cap becomes advisory rather than absolute.
policy.hardStopAboveCapNote: Hard stop is set to {{pct}}% but overage is off, so reservations still cannot exceed 100% of the budget. Enable overage if you intend to allow spending past the cap.

fields.notifyEnabled: Notify me as spend approaches the cap
fields.notifyPctHelp: Sends a notification once. Turn the checkbox off to never notify.
fields.stopProvisionPctHelp: No new instances are launched past this point. Running instances continue.
fields.drainPctHelp: No new work is dispatched; in-flight chunks are allowed to finish.
fields.hardStopPctHelp: Instances are destroyed immediately, finishing or not.
fields.drainTimeoutHelp: How long an instance may keep finishing its chunk before it is destroyed anyway.
fields.allowOverageHelp: Leave off to make the cap absolute. With it off, a $10 budget stops at $10.

errors.notifyRange: The notify threshold must be between 1% and the stop-provisioning threshold.
errors.stopBeforeDrain: The stop-provisioning threshold must not exceed the drain threshold.
errors.drainBeforeHardStop: The drain threshold must not exceed the hard-stop threshold.
errors.negativeTimeout: The drain timeout must not be negative.

fleet.title: Cloud Fleet
fleet.description: Every rented instance that may still be costing money.
fleet.empty: No instances are running. Nothing is being billed.
fleet.destroyFailed: The provider refused to destroy this instance — it is still billing
fleet.destroyBody: Destroy "{{label}}" now? Billing stops as soon as the provider confirms.
fleet.destroyJobWarning: This instance is working a job. Its in-flight chunk is lost and will be re-dispatched elsewhere.
fleet.teardownFailingBody: {{count}} instance(s) could not be destroyed and are still accruing cost. Check the provider console.
fleet.teardownFailingTooltip: Teardown failed; this instance is still billing
fleet.estimatedTooltip: Estimated from elapsed time and rate; the provider's own figure lands later.

rules.title: Wanneer het systeem mag uitgeven
rules.description: Budgetten bepalen hoeveel er mag worden uitgegeven. Deze regels bepalen wanneer er überhaupt iets mag worden uitgegeven. Zonder deze regels huurt de autoscaler al na één tick zonder voortgang, voor elke job, op elk uur, zonder plafond per job.
rules.inheritBody: Klanten erven elk veld afzonderlijk, dus een hier aangescherpte standaard bereikt elke klant die juist dat veld niet heeft overschreven. Overschrijvingen per klant worden op het klantscherm bewerkt.

helperText.minJobPriority: Absolute prioriteit, geen percentage. Uw huidige plafond is {{ceiling}}.
helperText.floorOff: Geen ondergrens: elke job met cloud burst komt in aanmerking voor automatische provisioning.
helperText.minStarvation: Hoe lang een job helemaal geen voortgang moet maken voordat betaalde capaciteit wordt gehuurd. 0 huurt bij de eerste tick. Geldt alleen voor de autoscaler.
helperText.skipIfFinishing: Niet huren voor een job die naar verwachting binnen deze tijd klaar is op bestaande capaciteit — een gehuurde instance heeft 5 tot 10 minuten nodig om op te starten en te synchroniseren. 0 slaat nooit over.
helperText.maxSpendPerJob: Plafond voor cloud-uitgaven van één job over de hele levensduur, niet per maand. Leeg betekent geen plafond. Geldt overal, ook bij handmatige provisioning door een beheerder.
helperText.windowEnabled: Geldt alleen voor starts. Instances worden nooit afgebroken omdat het venster sluit — TTL en idle drain doen dat.
helperText.windowTz: IANA-naam, bijv. America/Chicago. Leeg laten voor UTC.
helperText.windowWrap: Een sluitingstijd vóór de openingstijd loopt over middernacht, wat de normale manier is om "alleen 's nachts huren" te schrijven. Beide gelijk betekent altijd open.

system.ceilingsHelp: Absolute system-wide limits, applied before any client budget is consulted.
system.workHelp: How much work a rented instance is given at a time, and how quickly an idle one is released. Per-chunk overhead is billed at rental rates, so these trade throughput against waste.
system.reconciliationHelp: How often the database is checked against what the provider is actually running, and how long an unrecognised instance is tolerated before it is destroyed.
system.capDisabledWarning: Cloud provisioning is currently DISABLED: the global monthly cap is 0. Providers, client budgets and cloud-enabled jobs will all be configured correctly and nothing will ever be rented. Set a non-zero cap to enable it.

fields.monthlyCapHelp: Across all clients and providers. 0 disables cloud provisioning entirely — it is not unlimited.
fields.concurrentCapHelp: Maximum rented instances at once, across every provider and client. 0 means unlimited, still bounded by budgets and provider quotas.
fields.defaultMaxInstancesPerJobHelp: Maximaal aantal gehuurde instanties voor een taak die geen eigen limiet instelt. Leeg betekende voorheen onbeperkt, waardoor in een cloud-only omgeving alleen het klantbudget voorkomt dat een wachtende taak elke minuut opnieuw huurt. Een waarde op de taak zelf gaat nog steeds voor. 0 herstelt onbeperkt.
fields.chunkDurationHelp: Minimale chunkduur voor cloudagents. Een gehuurde GPU wordt in rekening gebracht terwijl hashcat opstart, kernels autotunet en de woordenlijst laadt, dus cloudchunks worden opgetrokken naar deze waarde, ook als de taak om minder vraagt. Een taak die om MEER vraagt behoudt zijn eigen waarde. Wordt altijd teruggebracht tot de resterende levensduur van de instantie. 0 schakelt de ondergrens uit.
fields.teardownSlackHelp: Reserved at the end of an instance's lifetime for drain and destroy, so a chunk is never planned past the point the instance dies.
fields.idleDrainHelp: Destroy a rented instance after this long with no pending work. Bounds how much you pay for a GPU that has run out of things to do.
fields.commissioningGraceHelp: Vernietig een gehuurde instantie die nooit een taak heeft gekregen na deze tijd, gemeten vanaf het moment dat de agent zich registreerde. Een koude instantie moet eerst haar bestanden downloaden en een benchmark uitvoeren, dus een waarde onder ongeveer 20 minuten vernietigt gezonde instanties tijdens het opstarten — en omdat de taak nog wacht, wordt er meteen een nieuwe gehuurd. 0 schakelt dit uit.
fields.reaperIntervalHelp: How often to reconcile the database against provider inventory and destroy anything that should not exist.
fields.orphanGraceHelp: Destroy instances found on the provider account with no matching database row after this long. This is the only recovery for a launch whose record never landed.
fields.agentImageHelp: e.g. zerkereod/krakenhashes-agent-cloud:cloud-gpu. Leave blank to fall back to KH_CLOUD_AGENT_IMAGE, then to the built-in default. Note the built-in default is :latest, which only exists once a release has been tagged — pre-release deployments must set this.
fields.defaultBurstEnabled: Cloud burst inschakelen voor elke taak
fields.defaultBurstEnabledHelp: Behandelt elke taak als cloud-burst-geschikt, zonder het vinkje op elke preset, workflow en taak te zetten. Bedoeld voor implementaties zonder eigen GPU's, waar huren de enige manier is om werk uit te voeren. Clientbudgetten en instantielimieten blijven gelden. Werkt direct, ook voor taken die al in de wachtrij staan.
fields.defaultClientHelp: Clouduitgaven voor een hashlijst zonder eigen client worden hier in rekening gebracht. Op Geen laten betekent dat niet-toegewezen werk helemaal geen capaciteit kan huren. Budgetten, instantielimieten en de drempelladder gelden gewoon voor de gekozen client — een client met de naam "Niet toegewezen werk" houdt het uitgavenrapport eerlijk.
fields.defaultClientNone: Geen — niet-toegewezen werk kan de cloud niet gebruiken
fields.crackDrainGraceHelp: Wacht voordat een gehuurde instantie wordt vernietigd zo lang tot een taak die deze nog bezit klaar is met het uploaden van gekraakte wachtwoorden. Gemeten vanaf de laatste schrijfactie van die taak, niet vanaf de start, zodat een werkende agent nooit wordt vernietigd en op een vastgelopen agent niet eindeloos wordt gewacht. Moet langer zijn dan de idle drain en korter dan 30 minuten. 0 vernietigt direct, wat al gevonden cracks blijvend kan verliezen — ze kunnen niet opnieuw worden verzonden vanaf een machine die niet meer bestaat.

system.agentHelp: The container image rented instances pull and run. It must be a tag that exists in the registry: a missing tag is not a startup error — the instance boots, the pull fails, and the host self-terminates about a minute later, billed.
system.eligibilityHelp: Of taken überhaupt in aanmerking komen om capaciteit te huren. Alles hierboven begrenst wat er uitgegeven mag worden; dit bepaalt of er iets wordt uitgegeven.

serverCertificate.title: Server Certificate
serverCertificate.description: Manage the addresses the server's TLS certificate covers. Agents can only connect to an address listed here.

warning.title: KrakenHashes is an internal tool
warning.body: It must never be reachable from the public internet. It handles cracked credentials, so only private and VPN addresses can be added to the certificate — public IP addresses are rejected. If this deployment is exposed publicly, take it offline before continuing.

summary.title: Current certificate
summary.unavailable: The server certificate could not be read.
summary.subject: Subject
summary.coversNothing: This certificate lists no addresses at all. No agent can connect.
summary.pending: {{count}} address(es) have been saved but are not in the certificate yet. Click Apply & Reissue.
summary.deprecatedEnv: KH_ADDITIONAL_IP_ADDRESSES or KH_ADDITIONAL_DNS_NAMES is still set in the environment. It is no longer read — these settings replace it. Remove the variable to avoid confusion.

sans.title: Addresses this certificate should cover
sans.unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Click Apply & Reissue to put them into the certificate.
sans.lockedTooltip: Always included. Removing it would break the internal proxy and health checks.

ip.title: IP addresses
ip.help: Private and VPN addresses only: 10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x, 100.64–127.x (Tailscale, NetBird), link-local, and IPv6 ULA.

dns.title: DNS names
dns.help: Hostnames agents and browsers use to reach this server.

validation.public_ip: {{address}} is a public IP address and cannot be added. KrakenHashes is an internal-only tool. It handles cracked credentials and must never be reachable from the internet. Only private addresses (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x, 100.64–127.x, link-local and IPv6 ULA) can be added. If this is your VPN's address, the VPN is using address space that belongs to someone else on the internet — change its network range to a private or CGNAT range.
validation.bind_address: {{address}} is a bind address, not a reachable one. No client connects to it.
validation.multicast: {{address}} is a multicast address and cannot identify a server.
validation.has_port: Enter only the hostname, with no port.
validation.is_ip: That is an IP address. Add it to the IP address list instead.
validation.too_long: That name is longer than the 253-character limit.

discovered.title: Discovered addresses
discovered.help: Addresses seen reaching this server that the certificate does not cover. Nothing here is applied automatically.
discovered.empty: No addresses discovered yet. Start an agent, or open this page from the address your agents use, and it will appear here.
discovered.added: {{address}} added. Click Apply & Reissue to put it into the certificate.

sourceHelp.agent_tls_failure: An authenticated agent reported that it could not verify this server's certificate for this address.
sourceHelp.host_header: Observed in a request's Host header. Anyone who can reach this server can influence this value — confirm it before adding.
sourceHelp.tls_sni: Observed as the server name in a TLS handshake.

reissue.noChangeBody: The certificate already covers every configured address and is not close to expiry.
reissue.validUntil: The new certificate is valid until {{date}}.
reissue.backendReloaded: The API on port 31337 is already serving the new certificate. No restart was needed.
reissue.nginxReloaded: The web UI on port 443 was reloaded and is serving the new certificate.
reissue.nginxFailed: The web UI on port 443 is still serving the previous certificate
reissue.backup: Previous certificate material was backed up to {{path}}.
reissue.agentsReconnect: Agents that were failing will reconnect on their own within 30 seconds. No agent restart is needed.
reissue.agentsRefetch: Every agent must re-fetch the CA. Agents do this automatically the next time a handshake fails, but browsers that trusted the old CA must install the new one by hand.
reissue.nginxFailedBody: The API is already serving the new certificate, so agents are unaffected. The web UI on port 443 will keep presenting the previous one until KrakenHashes is restarted.

confirmRemoval.title: Remove addresses from the certificate?
confirmRemoval.body: The following addresses are in the current certificate and will be removed: {{addresses}}. Any agent connecting on one of them will stop being able to connect until it is added back.

rotateCa.title: Rotate the certificate authority
rotateCa.warning: Rotating the certificate authority issues a brand-new CA and re-signs the server and agent certificates. Every agent must re-download the CA before it can reconnect, and every browser that trusted the old CA will show warnings until the new ca.crt is installed. Only do this if the CA private key may have been exposed.

banner.title: {{count}} agent(s) cannot verify this server's certificate
banner.body: {{agents}} is connecting to {{address}}, which is not listed in the server certificate. It will keep retrying and cannot come online until the certificate is reissued.
